cpu_compatibility.arm64: ARMv8-A, no optional extensions; ARMv8.1-A is not assumed. LSE is therefore not an archive-wide prerequisite.
cpu_compatibility.armhf: ARMv7 + VFPv3-D16; NEON not required by generic archive.
cpu_compatibility.bcm6813_assessment: CPU baseline matches B53/Cortex-A53. Actual runtime validation on kernel9 remains separate from archive compatibility. Optimized local packages may use cortex-a53+crypto+crc after feature verification.
cpu_compatibility.note: Optional IFUNC implementations and BTI/PAC notes are not proof of an ARMv8.1/LSE-only baseline. Do not reject a library solely because disassembly contains optional ISA instructions.

glibc.source_minimum_kernel_option: --enable-kernel=3.2 from debian/sysdeps/linux.mk; upstream architecture floor may raise it.
glibc.conclusion: The official libc package does not impose Linux5.x minimum. This is not a promise that every Ubuntu package or service works on4.19. Custom BE98 glibc2.44 still needs Ubuntu-format rebuild/package integration and actual tests.
local_rebuild_contract: Use Debian/Ubuntu source packaging, symbols, triggers, maintainer scripts and dependency semantics; do not copy loose libc/ld binaries over dpkg-owned files.
Keep libc6, libc6-dev, libc-bin, libc-dev-bin and libc-gconv-modules-extra versions mutually consistent.

All coinstalled Multi-Arch:same libc6 architectures must use the same package version and identical shared-file content. Upgrade nativearm64 + anyenabledarmhf + customarmel in one coordinated transaction.
Preserve vendor armel library/runtime identity until actual ASUS blobs are validated. Newglibc success with a probe does not prove all vendor private symbols and dlopen plugins work.

details: ld.so remains reachable at ABI-defined /lib path through usrmerge symlink; the actual loader is in the matching multiarch directory.
Generic headers live under /usr/include and architecture-specific headers under /usr/include/<tuple>.
libc-bin owns /usr/sbin/ldconfig. Keep ld.so.conf.d, loader cache, libc linker scripts, crt objects, GCC search paths and pkg-config multiarch paths coherent.
Do not use /usr/lib64 or old /lib32 as the primary multiarch layout.

systemd.future_requirement_distinction: 259.5 NEWS announces Linux5.10/glibc2.34 as a planned v260 minimum. Do not apply systemd262 baseline as though it described Ubuntu26.04 systemd259.5.

exact_source_findings.finding: Retains fallback when STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT unavailable; prior262 firstboot blocker is not automatically applicable.
Probes memory_recursiveprot and memory_hugetlb_accounting; omits unsupported mount options.
pidfd_open error falls back only for resource exhaustion; ENOSYS propagates.

systemd.kernel9_status: Full systemd259 PID1 compatibility not established by this audit. Kernel9 time64 work does not implement pidfd; do not replace ASUS PID1 on the device before exact-package QEMU boot/service tests and kernel API backports. Existing systemd262 evidence shows API gaps but is not an actual259 test.
migration_rules: Use cgroupv2 as required by modern systemd; reconcile vendor cgroup ownership and Docker controllers.
Use native ASUS service units and explicitly retain network ownership; avoid enabling systemd-networkd, resolved or NetworkManager to take over existing router interfaces implicitly.
Kernel API backports must preserve proprietary module ABI and behavior; a fake uname or unconditional success stub is not a compatibility solution.

bootstrap.recommended: mmdebstrap --variant=essential --architectures=arm64 with apt, ca-certificates and ubuntu-keyring, signed resolute + resolute-updates + resolute-security, isolated output root. Run dpkg configure/apt tests in target architecture environment.
bootstrap.mirror_note: All three suites and both arm64/armhf package indices verified from this mirror. Official Canonical ARM summer2026 article says arm64 also moved to archive.ubuntu.com; keep armhf onports if choosing splitmirrors. Oneportsstanza is currently verified forboth.

Publish optimizedtoolchain/glibc/vendor packages from a signed local feed with explicit package pins and versioning.
Do not globally freeze security updates; pin only custom replacement packages.
No proposed/development suite needed for essentialbase. Backports can be opt-in later.
